title: Minimum Cost For Tickets
hints: you only ever need a decision on days you actually travel - what's the minimum cost to be covered through day d, for every day d up to the last travel day?
define dp[d] as the minimum cost to handle all travel needs up through day d. if day d is not a travel day, dp[d] = dp[d-1] (nothing to buy)
if day d is a travel day, you must be covered by some pass bought on or before d - dp[d] = min(dp[d-1] + cost1, dp[d-7] + cost7, dp[d-30] + cost30), clamping any negative day index to dp[0] = 0
this is unbounded knapsack in disguise: the three pass lengths are reusable 'items' and you're filling a timeline instead of a capacity

you don't need a dp entry for every single calendar day if travel days are sparse - you can instead index dp by travel day position and binary-search (or track a pointer) for 'the last travel day at least 7 (or 30) days before this one'
commonMistakes: assuming a pass must start exactly on a travel day rather than realizing dp[d-7] and dp[d-30] should look back from the current day regardless of whether those days themselves were travel days
clamping negative day indices incorrectly, e.g. treating dp[-3] as an error instead of dp[0] (no cost needed before day 1)
recomputing dp for every non-travel day when only decision points on actual travel days matter, wasting time and complicating the indexing

content.problemStatement:
You need to travel on certain days of the year, given as a sorted list of
distinct day numbers, `days`. You can buy travel passes of three kinds,
each covering a consecutive run of days starting from the day it's
bought:

- a 1-day pass
- a 7-day pass
- a 30-day pass

Their costs are given, in that order, as a list of three `costs`. Passes
can overlap and can be bought on any day, not just travel days.

**Return the minimum total cost to be covered on every day you need to travel.**
constraints: days is sorted in strictly increasing order
notes: travel days clustered close together, where a single wider pass covers several at once
travel days spread far apart, where buying 1-day passes individually is cheapest

sampleTestCases.explanation: a 7-day pass bought on day 1 covers days 1 through 7 for 7, another 1-day pass covers day 8 for 2, and a 1-day pass covers day 20 for 2, totaling 11
buying three separate 1-day passes costs 2+2+2 = 6, which beats a single 7-day pass costing 7
a single 1-day pass is the cheapest way to cover one travel day

optimal.time: O(last day) or O(number of travel days) depending on formulation
optimal.space: O(last day) or O(number of travel days)
optimal.pattern: knapsack (unbounded over pass durations - the 'items' are the three pass lengths, reusable, and you're minimizing cost to cover a set of required days)

bruteForce.approach: recursively decide, for the earliest uncovered travel day, which of the three pass durations to buy starting from it, and recurse on the first travel day left uncovered by that pass
bruteForce.time: exponential without caching, since the same 'first uncovered day' subproblem recurs
bruteForce.space: O(number of travel days) recursion depth
